extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and attorneys subject to USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for imposing reciprocal exclusion from practice before the USPTO based on state disciplinary action, including notice/service, opportunity to contest, factual showing required to avoid identical discipline, and post-exclusion obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for exclusion based on state disciplinary disbarment
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) by being disbarred on ethical grounds from the practice of law by a State authority (e.g., Supreme Court of Florida).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may impose exclusion from practice before the USPTO pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 when a practitioner has been disbarred or disciplined on ethical grounds by a state disciplinary authority. The Final Order explicitly states exclusion was ordered for violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5) because the practitioner was disbarred by the Supreme Court of Florida.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and service requirements for reciprocal-discipline proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' must be mailed (first-class certified mail, return receipt requested) to the address provided pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11; if mailed service fails, service by publication pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24(b) and 11.35(b) is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order in this matter was mailed by first-class certified mail to the street address on file and was returned 'ATTEMPTED, UNKNOWN.' The Office then used publication in the Official Gazette (per §§ 11.24(b) and 11.35(b)) notifying the respondent how to obtain a copy. Compliance with these notice/service procedures is a prerequisite to proceeding with reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to contest and required content of response
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may contest imposition of identical discipline by filing, within 40 days, a response containing all information believed sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order informed Respondent that to contest the exclusion he must file, within 40 days, a response containing all information he believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted based on any grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Failure to file such a response supports a determination there is no genuine issue of material fact and that exclusion is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for showing a genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid reciprocal imposition of identical discipline, the respondent must raise a genuine issue of material fact under the criteria set out in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order concludes under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) that there was no genuine issue of material fact because the respondent did not file a response. The referenced regulation defines the limited grounds on which a respondent may demonstrate that identical discipline would be unwarranted (e.g., lack of due process in the other proceeding, mistaken identity, or that the misconduct does not warrant the same discipline), so a respondent's submission must address those specific grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate exclusion and compliance obligations while excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: If exclusion is ordered, the respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office and must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states respondent is excluded beginning on the date of the Final Order and must comply with § 11.58 (which addresses duties of excluded practitioners, e.g., giving notice to clients and transferring files). The Order also grants limited recognition to practice for thirty (30) days solely to facilitate compliance with § 11.58(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to facilitate compliance with § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: A short, time-limited recognition to practice (here, thirty days) may be granted for the sole purpose of facilitating the excluded practitioner's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly grants limited recognition to practice beginning on the date the order is signed and expiring 30 days after that date, solely to permit the respondent to comply with duties enumerated in § 11.58(b) (e.g., notifying clients and making arrangements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate the respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates, and the respondent shall not use or obtain any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order mandates both administrative dissociation by the USPTO and substantive prohibitions on the respondent: (1) USPTO will dissociate names from customer numbers and PKI certificates; (2) respondent may not use any customer number or PKI certificate while excluded; and (3) respondent may not obtain a customer number or PKI certificate while excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public notice of discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette and make disciplinary decisions available in the OED Reading Room; notice must also be given to state disciplinary agencies, courts of admission, and the public in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires publication of the Final Order and the specified Official Gazette notice describing the reason for exclusion. It also directs the OED Director to give notice of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state of admission, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public (per § 11.59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedures and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon any request for reinstatement, the respondent must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly states respondent shall comply with § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement (§ 11.60 sets forth requirements and procedures for seeking reinstatement to practice before the USPTO after suspension or exclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying misconduct types that support state disbarment
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of conduct supporting disbarment included abandonment of representation (failure to appear at calendar call and scheduled trial) and failure to respond to judicial and bar inquiries regarding such failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Notice recites the Supreme Court of Florida's findings: in July 2008 the practitioner abandoned his representation of an incarcerated criminal defendant; did not respond to two inquiries from the judge seeking an explanation for failure to appear; and did not respond to a requirement for explanation from the Florida Bar. Such conduct formed the factual basis for state disbarment and thus for reciprocal exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59 (and related provisions such as §§ 11.35, 11.58, and 11.60).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites these statutes and regulations as the legal basis for imposing exclusion, publication of notices, service procedures, compliance obligations while excluded, and reinstatement procedures. Practitioners and OED staff should consult these provisions for detailed legal requirements and processes.
